source_text: IV. Galerius Maximus collocutus cum concilio sententiam vix et aegre dixit verbis huiusmodi: Diu sacrilega mente vixisti et plurimos nefariae tibi conspirationis homines adgregasti et inimicum te diis Romanis et sacris legibus constituisti, nec te pii et sacratissimi principes Valerianus et Gallienus Augusti et Valerianus nobilissimus Caesar ad sectam caeremoniarum suarum revocare potuerunt. et ideo cum sis nequissimorum criminum auctor et signifer deprehensus, eris ipse documento his quos scelere tuo tecum adgregasti: sanguine tuo sancietur disciplina. et his dictis decretum ex tabella recitavit: Thascium Cyprianum gladio animadverti placet. Cyprianus episcopus dixit: Deo gratias.
pass_a_gloss: Galerius Maximus, having conferred with the council, with difficulty and reluctantly pronounced sentence in words of this kind: you have lived long with sacrilegious mind and gathered to yourself very many men of an impious conspiracy and set yourself as an enemy to the Roman gods and the sacred laws, nor were the pious and most sacred emperors Valerian and Gallienus Augusti and Valerian the most noble Caesar able to recall you to the practice of their rites; and therefore since you have been caught as author and standard-bearer of most wicked crimes, you yourself will serve as a warning to those whom you gathered with you by your crime: discipline shall be sanctioned by your blood; and with these words spoken he read the decree from the tablet: it is decided that Thascius Cyprian be punished by the sword; Cyprian the bishop said: thanks be to God.
pass_b_english: Galerius Maximus conferred with his council and then pronounced the sentence, with difficulty and reluctance, in words of this kind: Long have you lived with a sacrilegious mind, and you have gathered to yourself a great many men in an impious conspiracy, and you have made yourself an enemy to the Roman gods and to the sacred laws, nor were the pious and most sacred emperors Valerian and Gallienus, the Augusti, and Valerian, the most noble Caesar, able to recall you to the observance of their rites.

Therefore, since you have been seized as the author and standard-bearer of most wicked crimes, you yourself shall become a warning to those whom you gathered to yourself by your crime, and discipline shall be sealed by your blood.
When he had spoken these words, he read out the decree from the tablet: It is resolved that Thascius Cyprian shall be punished by the sword.
Cyprian the bishop said: Thanks be to God.

lemmas.gloss: to be punished by judicial action

choices.why: vix qualifies the act of speaking and aegre adds unwillingness, so both adverbs describe the pronouncement itself

choices.english: it is resolved that he be punished by the sword
choices.why: placet is the formal council decree formula and gladio specifies execution, while animadverti is the judicial euphemism for punishment
rejected: it pleases that attention be paid by the sword

choices.why: ablative/dative of recipient with implied giving, a set confessional response rather than thanks to the judge
